extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers studying functional analysis/convex analysis (reading exercise solutions)
extracted.subtask_description: Worked solutions and remarks for exercises in a functional/convex analysis textbook, covering separation theorems, conjugation, inf-convolution, monotone operators, Banach space theorems, and weak topologies. Used as worked examples and reference for proving standard propositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bipolar / separation argument for cone C
rubrics_metrics.description: C ⊂ C'' and C'' is closed. Conversely, if x0 ∈ C'' and x0 ∉ C then one may strictly separate {x0} and C (exist f0 and α0 with ⟨f0,x⟩ < α0 < ⟨f0,x0⟩ ∀x∈C), leading to a contradiction; hence membership in the bipolar forces membership in C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses Hahn–Banach separation and the fact 0∈C to renormalize the separating functional; standard bipolar/separation argument showing closure properties of polars/bipolars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polar of a linear subspace equals its annihilator
rubrics_metrics.description: If C is a linear subspace then C' = {f ∈ E' ; ⟨f,x⟩ = 0 ∀x ∈ C} = C^⊥.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identification of the polar/dual cone of a subspace with its orthogonal annihilator; useful when applying duality to subspaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collection of example convex functions (ϕ examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: A list of concrete examples of convex functions ϕ(f) (cases (a)–(l)) including indicator functions, entropy f log f − f, absolute value |f|, constant 0, −1 − log|f| on domains, sqrt(1+f^2), piecewise quadratic, p-power functions, and combinations with +∞ outside domains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides prototypical convex functions and domain descriptions; use these as test-cases when checking conjugation, lower semicontinuity, and domain issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conjugate functions on ℓ^p-type spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: Formulas and domain conditions for conjugates defined on sequence spaces (‖f‖_p finite etc.), giving expressions such as sums of ak|fk|^{k/(k−1)} under integrability conditions, and +∞ otherwise; references to the p and conjugate p' relation (1/p + 1/p' =1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit conjugation computations for sequence norms and weighted sums; check integrability conditions (summability of appropriate powers) to decide finiteness of conjugate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicator function conjugacy and examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples where ϕ = I_A with specified set A (e.g., A = {[f1,f2]; f1 ≤0, f2 ≤0, and 4f1f2 ≥ 1}) and computations showing ϕ^* = I_{D^⊥} for appropriate D, and pathological sup/inf behaviours (e.g., ϕ(-f)+ψ^*(f)=+∞ ∀f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows how indicator functions map under Fenchel conjugation to indicators of orthogonal complements or related sets; watch for lack of regularity that invalidates Fenchel-Moreau hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convexity and Lipschitz property of distance-to-set function φ(x)=inf_{a∈A}||x−a||
rubrics_metrics.description: Triangle inequality yields φ(x) ≤ ||x−y|| + φ(y). Using that and exchanging x,y yields Lipschitz-like bounds; φ is convex if A is convex, and A = {x; φ(x) ≤ 0} when A is closed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distance-to-set maps are 1-Lipschitz and convexity of A ↔ convexity of φ; standard manipulation via convex combinations and infimum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inf-convolution conjugacy identity (ϕ⊙ψ)^* = ϕ^* + ψ^*
rubrics_metrics.description: For proper convex lower semicontinuous ϕ,ψ the conjugate of the inf-convolution equals the sum of the conjugates: (ϕ∇ψ)^*(f) = ϕ^*(f) + ψ^*(f), and related sup–inf equalities (Fenchel-type identities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof via standard manipulations of suprema: express conjugates as sup_{x} {⟨f,x⟩ − ϕ(x)} etc., use decompositions x = (x−y)+y and Theorem 1.12 (Fenchel–Moreau).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual formula for infimum of sum and Fenchel duality (S1 equality)
rubrics_metrics.description: For given f ∈ E' sup_{x∈E} {⟨f,x⟩ − ϕ(x) − ψ(x)} = inf_{g∈E'} {ϕ^*(f−g) + ψ^*(g)} (the min–max representation and Fenchel duality for convolution).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate sup over x into −inf over x of shifted ϕ and apply Fenchel–Moreau (Theorem 1.12); useful for proving existence of minimizers and dual equalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moreau–Yosida envelope properties (ϕ_n)
rubrics_metrics.description: Properties of ϕ_n defined by inf-convolution with quadratic term: existence of affine minorants ensuring ϕ_n > −∞; ϕ_n convex; Lipschitz bound |ϕ_n(x1) − ϕ_n(x2)| ≤ n||x1 − x2||; (ϕ_n)^* = I_{nB} + ϕ^*; monotone convergence liminf_n ϕ_n(x) ≥ ϕ(x) and in fact ϕ_n ↗ ϕ pointwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard Moreau envelope facts: use convexity/inf-convolution properties and lower-semicontinuity to pass to limits; the Lipschitz and proximal properties are essential in regularization arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of a supporting functional f0 ∈ F(x) via Fenchel duality
rubrics_metrics.description: Given x and certain convex functions ϕ,ψ constructed (quadratic + indicator), Theorem 1.12 yields f0 ∈ E' such that ϕ^*(f0)+ψ^*(−f0)=0, which implies f0 ∈ F(x) and equality conditions (norm equalities etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct ϕ and ψ suitably (one quadratic, one indicator) so that inf_z {ϕ(z)+ψ(z)} = 0 and invoke Fenchel duality to obtain dual element realizing primal equality; classical way to produce dual elements attaining support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Baire category to deduce local boundedness of convex l.s.c. functions
rubrics_metrics.description: If ϕ is l.s.c. and D(ϕ) has nonempty interior then using Baire category on level sets one shows existence of a ball on which ϕ is bounded above by a constant, leading to local boundedness and related estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard argument: cover a ball by closed level sets Fn and use that some Fn has nonempty interior; used to deduce continuity at interior points or Lipschitz-type bounds on small balls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic seminorm properties and limit arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: For a seminorm p verifying subadditivity and homogeneity properties, p(0)=0; convergence p(α_n x_n)→0 under given assumptions; various limit manipulations using triangle inequality and subsequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elementary but important checks when verifying seminorm continuity and behavior under sequences; useful in topological vector space arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation of a bilinear form as a bounded linear operator
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a bilinear continuous form a(x,y) satisfying hypotheses, there exists T ∈ L(E,F') such that a(x,y) = ⟨Tx,y⟩_F' for all x,y, and verifying boundedness of T requires checking images of unit ball are bounded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard Riesz-type representation in Banach space settings for bilinear forms; boundedness often follows from corollaries (e.g., Corollary 2.5) or uniform boundedness principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boundedness and closedness results for monotone operators
rubrics_metrics.description: Monotonicity inequalities yield bounds like ⟨Ax_n, x_n⟩ ≤ ε_n||Ax_n|| + C(x), from which boundedness of (Ax_n) follows; closedness of graph of T and properties of A imply various boundedness/closure contradictions when assuming unbounded sequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use monotonicity together with auxiliary estimates and contradiction to show sequences cannot blow up; routine for maximal monotone operator theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closed graph → closed operator and tests for closedness
rubrics_metrics.description: Method: show graph of T is closed by taking xn→x and T xn → f and passing limit in monotonicity inequality to obtain f = Tx; this proves T is closed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prove closedness of operator graphs by taking limits in defining inequalities; typical in monotone operator and PDE contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalence of closedness of image T(M) and closedness of M+N(T)
rubrics_metrics.description: If T(M) is closed then M + N(T) = T^{-1}(T(M)) is closed. Conversely, if M + N(T) is closed and T is surjective then T(M) is closed (open mapping theorem used to show image is open/closed appropriately).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful criterion when analyzing ranges of bounded operators and decompositions by kernel; apply open mapping theorem when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of the open mapping theorem: existence of bounded right-inverses and basis preimages
rubrics_metrics.description: If T is surjective between Banach spaces then there exists c>0 with T(B_E) ⊃ c B_F. Using this, one can choose preimages of canonical basis elements with bounded norms and construct left or right inverses or maps with desired mapping properties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard functional analytic construction: open mapping ensures lower bounds on operator norms on complements; used to build explicit bounded lifts and sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stability of invertibility under small perturbations (Banach fixed-point argument)
rubrics_metrics.description: If T is invertible with bounded inverse T^{-1}, then T+U is invertible for any U with ||T^{-1}||·||U|| <1; proof uses contraction mapping rewriting x = T^{-1}(f − Ux).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classical Neumann series / fixed-point argument for perturbation of invertible operators; provides neighborhood of invertible operators in operator norm topology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closed range characterization via distance estimate on quotient
rubrics_metrics.description: For quotient π: E→E/N(T), R(T) is closed iff there exists C such that dist(x,N(T)) ≤ C||Tx|| ∀x∈E (equivalently ||πx|| ≤ C|| (˜T)πx||), i.e., lower bound estimate holds on quotient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key equivalence used to detect closed range: a bounded below property on quotient or equivalently inverse boundedness on the induced injective map.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orthogonality relations: N(A) ⊂ R(A)⊥ and quantitative graph estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: If u ∈ N(A) and v ∈ D(A) then ⟨Au,v⟩ = 0, hence N(A) ⊂ R(A)⊥. Furthermore, using open mapping on A:D(A)→R(A) one gets estimates like ⟨Au,u⟩ ≥ −C||Au||^2 for u∈D(A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combines algebraic orthogonality of kernel with closed-range/open mapping estimates to bound quadratic forms; used in operator theory and PDE coercivity arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual conjugation under linear map T and minimization over kernel of adjoint
rubrics_metrics.description: For ϕ(f) = sup_{x} {⟨f,x⟩ − ϕ(x)} and a linear map T, one gets formula ϕ^*(T^*f) = min_{h∈N(T^*)} ψ^*(f − h) (i.e., conjugate after precomposition by T reduces to a minimization over the kernel of T^*).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful identity when pushing conjugation through linear operators; derive by writing sup over range and using indicator functions for R(T) and Theorem 1.12.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mazur's lemma / convex closure of weakly convergent sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: If x_n → x weakly then conv{x_n, x_{n+1}, ...} has closure containing x (Mazur): there exists sequence of convex combinations y_n ∈ conv{x_n,...,x_{m(n)}} with y_n → x strongly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructive method to pass from weak to strong convergence via convex combinations; widely used in variational methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weak compactness of unit ball and attainment of supremum in reflexive strictly convex spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: If E is reflexive (and strictly convex) then sup_{x∈B_E} ⟨f,x⟩ is attained at a unique x0 ∈ B_E; duality map yields uniqueness of supporting point and characterization f∈F(x).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use reflexivity to get compactness in weak topology, then strict convexity to guarantee uniqueness of maximizer; standard in convex optimization and duality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strict convexity of constructed dual norms and uniqueness in projection problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Define auxiliary strictly convex norms (e.g., |f|_2 from a weighted ℓ^2 of evaluations) to obtain strict convexity of combined norms (||·||^2 + |·|^2) and deduce uniqueness of minimizers and dual elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique: combine norms to enforce strict convexity, then apply uniqueness and minimization arguments (used to show duality mapping is single-valued).
